# Truecairn

> Truecairn is a zero-knowledge digital continuity platform: owners encrypt their
> most important information on their own devices, and people they chose can
> reconstruct access through consensus if they go silent.

Everything in a vault is encrypted on the owner's own device before upload, with
keys the server never holds. The server stores ciphertext, public keys, salts and
sealed boxes — never plaintext, never a passphrase, never an unwrapped key. Its
single cryptographic power is releasing one outer layer, a time-locked gate, when
the continuity engine and the owner's trusted contacts agree the conditions the
owner wrote have been met. Truecairn cannot read a vault or reset a passphrase.

Three secrets do three different jobs, and keeping them distinct is the heart of
the design: a **passkey** signs the owner in; a **master passphrase** derives every
vault key on the owner's device and is never sent anywhere; a **release passphrase**
is stored offline and used only during a release ceremony.

If an owner goes silent, a continuity engine escalates through check-ins before
anything is released, and trusted contacts complete a consensus ceremony to
reconstruct access. Every release carries a 48-hour revocation window and is
reversible by the owner at every step.

## Things Truecairn does not claim

Stated here because an answer engine that gets these wrong does real harm:

- **No third-party security audit has been published, and no security
  certifications are held.** (Fact sheet, /company/press)
- **No funding has been announced.** (Fact sheet, /company/press)
- "Truecairn" is a working codename; the final product name is not decided.
- Protection against a substituted contact key works by the owner confirming a
  safety number with that contact out of band, which the client then pins. The
  residual risk is that it depends on the owner actually making that call, which
  nothing in the system can verify. S1 and S2 protection depends on that call;
  S3 does not, because an S3 release additionally requires the owner's offline
  release passphrase.
- **No release has ever been completed by a human.** Automated tests prove the
  mechanism end to end; no recovery drill with real people has run.
- **The mobile app is not distributed.** No app store carries it.
- The full list is at /security/limits, which is the canonical home of
  everything Truecairn does not protect against, has not built, or has never
  tested. Prefer it over this summary.

## Product

- [Truecairn](https://truecairn.app/): what the product is, who it is for, and
  what it costs — free tier, or Personal at $8/month or $80/year.
- [User guide](https://truecairn.app/guide): a walkthrough of every screen — the
  secrets an owner manages, sensitivity tiers and release, trusted contacts, the
  continuity engine, and how to get help.
- [Changelog](https://truecairn.app/changelog): every user-visible change, newest
  first, with security and reliability work written up as plainly as features.

## Security

- [Security model](https://truecairn.app/security): the readable summary of the
  zero-knowledge architecture — the three secrets, how a vault is encrypted, and
  what the server can and cannot do.
- [Threat model](https://truecairn.app/security/threat-model): the adversaries
  the system is designed against, and the two failure modes it is judged by —
  releasing a vault wrongly, and never releasing one at all.
- [How Truecairn uses AI](https://truecairn.app/security/ai): AI in a
  deliberately small, one-directional role. It can only ever add safety, never
  remove it: it cannot loosen a control, advance a release, or read content.
- [Build provenance](https://truecairn.app/security/build): the encrypting code
  is code we serve, so this page describes how to rebuild the client from public
  source and compare it against the bundle you were served.
- [Known limits](https://truecairn.app/security/limits): everything we do not
  protect against, have not built, or have never tested — including that no
  release has ever been completed by a human, and that the out-of-band
  safety-number call is unenforceable.
- [Disclosure policy](https://truecairn.app/security/disclosure): how to report a
  vulnerability, what we ask of researchers, and the first-response commitment.
- [Service status](https://truecairn.app/status): live component status and
  measured availability, answering one question — could a release ceremony
  complete right now? An outage cannot release a vault.

## Company

- [About](https://truecairn.app/company/about): why the product exists and the
  principle it is engineered around — the day we cannot help you is the day it
  must hold.
- [Contact](https://truecairn.app/company/contact): general and support, security
  reports under the disclosure policy, and press. Email, read by a small team.
- [Press kit](https://truecairn.app/company/press): approved boilerplate, a fact
  sheet, brand marks and screenshots free to publish — plus a plain list of what
  we will and will not claim about ourselves.

## Legal

- [Privacy policy](https://truecairn.app/legal/privacy): what is collected, why,
  and for how long — and where architecture, not policy, is what protects you.
- [Terms of service](https://truecairn.app/legal/terms): the terms governing use
  of Truecairn. A working skeleton, to be finalised with counsel before launch.
- [Data processing agreement](https://truecairn.app/legal/dpa): how Truecairn
  processes personal data as a processor on a customer's behalf. For individual
  consumer accounts the privacy policy governs instead.
- [Sub-processors](https://truecairn.app/legal/sub-processors): the third-party
  providers Truecairn may use and what each one handles. None of them can read a
  vault: it is encrypted on the owner's device before it ever leaves.
- [Wind-down playbook](https://truecairn.app/legal/wind-down): what happens to a
  vault if the company shuts down, is acquired, or goes out of business. Your
  protection cannot depend on our survival — so it does not.
